questions.question: The axilla is described as a fat-filled space of which shape?
questions.explanation: The axilla is described as a fat-filled pyramid-shaped space.

questions.question: Where is the axilla located?
options: Between the upper arm and chest wall
Between the forearm and chest wall
questions.explanation: The axilla is located between the upper part of the arm and the side of the chest wall.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is NOT contained within the axilla?
questions.explanation: The axilla contains the brachial plexus, axillary vessels, and lymph nodes. The femoral artery is in the lower limb.

questions.question: The axillary lymph nodes within the axilla primarily drain which regions?
questions.explanation: Groups of lymph nodes within the axilla drain the upper limb and the breast.

questions.question: Why is the axilla clinically important during physical examination?
options: It is a common site for fractures
Axillary lymph nodes are often enlarged
It is the origin of the sciatic nerve
questions.explanation: The axillary lymph nodes are often enlarged and hence routinely palpated during physical examination.

questions.question: The axilla resembles a truncated four-sided pyramid and presents an apex, a base, and how many walls?
questions.explanation: The axilla presents an apex, a base, and four walls (anterior, posterior, medial, and lateral).

questions.question: The apex of the axilla is also known as what?
questions.explanation: The apex is also termed the cervico-axillary canal.

questions.question: The apex of the axilla is bounded anteriorly by which structure?
questions.explanation: The apex is bounded in front by the clavicle.

questions.question: The apex of the axilla is bounded posteriorly by which structure?
questions.explanation: The apex is bounded behind by the upper border of the scapula.

questions.question: The apex of the axilla is bounded medially by which structure?
options: Outer border of the first rib
questions.explanation: The apex is bounded medially by the outer border of the first rib.

questions.question: Which structures pass through the cervico-axillary canal to enter the axilla from the neck?
questions.explanation: The axillary artery and brachial plexus enter the axilla from the neck through this gap.

questions.question: The base or floor of the axilla is formed by which structure?
questions.explanation: The base is at the lower end of the axilla and is formed by the axillary fascia.

questions.question: The anterior axillary fold is formed by the lower border of which muscle?
questions.explanation: The anterior axillary fold is formed by the lower border of the pectoralis major muscle.

questions.question: The posterior axillary fold is formed by which muscles?
questions.explanation: The posterior axillary fold is formed by the tendon of latissimus dorsi and teres major muscles.

questions.question: The perpendicular line dropped midway between the anterior and posterior axillary folds is called what?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular line dropped from a point midway between the anterior and posterior axillary folds is called the midaxillary line.

questions.question: The anterior wall of the axilla is formed by all of the following muscles EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: The anterior wall is formed by the pectoralis major, subclavius, and pectoralis minor. The subscapularis forms the posterior wall.

questions.question: The posterior wall of the axilla is formed by which muscle above?
questions.explanation: The posterior wall is formed by the subscapularis muscle above.

questions.question: The posterior wall of the axilla is formed by which muscles below?
questions.explanation: The posterior wall is formed by the latissimus dorsi and teres major muscles below.

questions.question: The medial wall of the axilla is formed by the upper four or five ribs and which muscle?
questions.explanation: The medial wall is formed by the upper four or five ribs and corresponding intercostal spaces covered by the serratus anterior muscle.

questions.question: The lateral wall of the axilla is formed by the tendon of which muscle in the bicipital groove?
questions.explanation: The lateral wall is formed by the tendon of biceps brachii in the bicipital groove of the humerus.

questions.question: Which other muscle, besides the short head of the biceps brachii, forms the lateral wall?
questions.explanation: The lateral wall is formed by the coracobrachialis and short head of the biceps brachii.

questions.question: Why is the lateral wall of the axilla described as extremely narrow?
options: It is covered by thick fat
Anterior and posterior walls converge there
It is made only of fascia
questions.explanation: The lateral wall is extremely narrow because the anterior and posterior walls of the axilla converge at this site.

questions.question: The axilla acts as a funnel-shaped tunnel for what structures?
questions.explanation: It acts as a funnel-shaped tunnel for neurovascular structures to pass from the root of the neck to the upper limb.

questions.question: The axillary vein enters the neck from the axilla through which structure?
questions.explanation: The axillary vein enters the neck from the axilla through the cervico-axillary canal.

questions.question: The base of the axilla is directed in which direction?
questions.explanation: The base is at the lower end of the axilla and directed downwards.

questions.question: What forms the medial boundary of the base of the axilla?
options: Lateral aspect of the chest wall
questions.explanation: The base is bounded medially by the lateral aspect of the chest wall.

questions.question: The apex of the axilla is directed towards which region?
questions.explanation: The apex is directed upwards and medially into the root of the neck.

questions.question: Which important surface landmark is associated with the base of the axilla?
questions.explanation: The midaxillary line is an important surface landmark related to the base of the axilla.

questions.question: Pus formation in this region is common and is referred to as what?
questions.explanation: The text notes that an abscess in this region is also common.

questions.question: The anterior and posterior walls of the axilla converge at which wall?
questions.explanation: The lateral wall is extremely narrow because the anterior and posterior walls of the axilla converge at this site.
